workspace.name: UnityIndie RPG MMO
workspace.note: The workspace root is NOT a git repo. Each repo below is independent.

tiers.fast: Always required for every touched module and every module that depends on it. Cheap, local, deterministic.
tiers.extended: Required when a trigger applies, but expensive or environment-sensitive. Ask the user before running; otherwise report NOT RUN (needs confirmation).
tiers.external: Runs outside this shell (Unity Editor, CI, Docker stack, remote). Ask, or report NOT RUN (external) with the reason.

go.note: go.mod requires go 1.26.x; GOTOOLCHAIN=auto downloads/uses the cached toolchain, so a lower local go is fine unless GOTOOLCHAIN=local.

dotnet.note: WSL usually has only the Windows dotnet.exe. Substitute {dotnet} with the resolved binary.

protoc.note: CI pins protoc + protoc-gen-go at the CI pins (facts protoc-ci-pin, protoc-gen-go-ci-pin). Regenerating with another version drifts the committed headers and fails the proto-generated CI job.

unity-mcp.purpose: Unity Editor MCP (ai-game-developer). Reachable only while the Editor has the client project open. Used to run the Unity Test Runner from an agent.

comfyui.purpose: ComfyUI started headless (main.py, default port). asset-gen runs workflows on it through comfy-mcp; reachable only while ComfyUI runs.

comfyui-desktop.purpose: ComfyUI Desktop session (its own port). Either this or the headless comfyui service is enough for comfy-mcp.

dev_tools.provides: Unity Editor from the agent (ai-game-developer, client .mcp.json): tests-run (EditMode/PlayMode, filter by assembly/class/method), console logs, asset and scene edits (human gate unity-asset-edit).
dev_tools.fallback: Unity tests stay HUMAN_REQUIRED (Editor) or CI; never hand-edit scene/prefab YAML

dev_tools.provides: Go code intelligence over gopls (agent-lsp `lsp` server in the workspace/server .mcp.json): blast_radius, find_references, callers before changing an exported Go symbol or interface.
dev_tools.fallback: grep for the symbol plus go vet / go build of every module that depends on shared

dev_tools.provides: C# code intelligence for the game server, Shared.GameLogic and the com.cuvara.* packages (none configured yet, known issue no-csharp-lsp).
dev_tools.fallback: grep for the symbol plus {dotnet} build of the solution (server) or an Editor compile through unity-mcp (packages, client)

dev_tools.provides: PostgreSQL documentation search (search_docs) for SQL migrations, indexes and locking behaviour.
dev_tools.fallback: the PostgreSQL manual for the server's Postgres version

dev_tools.provides: Keeps long build, test and benchmark logs out of the conversation (ctx_execute / ctx_batch_execute return only the derived answer).
dev_tools.fallback: pipe logs through tail / grep for the summary lines; run-checks.py already stores full logs as evidence

dev_tools.provides: Independent second diagnosis or implementation pass (codex:rescue) for a stuck bug; its output is reviewed like any other diff and is outside the Factory hooks. For asset-gen: the independent prompt and image review (codex exec, read-only sandbox) of a generation run.
dev_tools.fallback: none needed; asset-gen: a Claude review recorded as SAME_MODEL:claude (grades WARN, never PASS)

dev_tools.provides: Codex in-session subagents for Codex task sessions: multi_agent on and the subagent model inside pipeline.models.scope, read from two config keys only (agents.default_subagent_model, agents.subagent.model).
dev_tools.fallback: set [agents] default_subagent_model to the pipeline.subagents codex model in the Codex config and run codex features enable multi_agent; Claude-only runs need nothing

dev_tools.provides: Build and test the C# game server, Shared.GameLogic and the Netcode headless tests (Windows dotnet.exe on WSL, known issue dotnet-wsl).
Build, vet and test the Go gateway, shared, nakama and integration_test modules.
Regenerate wire bindings with generate.sh (CI pins libprotoc 29.3, fact protoc-ci-pin).
dev_tools.fallback: let CI regenerate; a local protoc that differs from the pin drifts the generated code

dev_tools.provides: Image builds, the compose stack (stack.sh) and Docker-backed integration tests.

dotnet-counters / dotnet-trace: live GC, allocation-rate and thread-pool counters and CPU sampling traces of a running game server process (JIT build; NativeAOT supports EventPipe counters only partially).
dev_tools.fallback: the server's own OTel metrics on /metrics (gameserver.gc.*, gameserver.tick.duration, gameserver.sim.group.duration) and the BENCH_TICK micro-benches; say which was used

dev_tools.provides: Figma file access for UI work: get_metadata (frame tree and node ids), get_screenshot (reference image), get_variable_defs (variable collections and modes). Read-only use in ui-figma-import step 1. The mcp: probe reads only .mcp.json and ~/.claude.json, so a claude.ai connector server (claude_ai_Figma, configured on the account) shows MISSING while it is usable in the session.
dev_tools.fallback: ask the user for the frame link (Copy link to selection, with node-id=) and a PNG export of the frame; the preflight is then HUMAN_REQUIRED for anything the screenshot cannot show (variable bindings)

dev_tools.provides: rpg-factory testlab (testlab/testlab.py, bundled with this plugin): autonomous multi-client runs with real rendered Unity clients against a local stack - scenarios S01.., suites, sweeps, and re-analysis of a stored run's evidence (analyze, replay-trace, thresholds, leak-check).
dev_tools.fallback: the hand-walked multi-client steps in measure references/legs.md; a claim the run did not produce stays NOT_RUN

dev_tools.provides: ComfyUI from the agent through the official Comfy-Org comfy-mcp server (tool ids mcp__comfy-mcp__<tool>): server_info, validate_workflow against the live node list, run_workflow, job, fetch_outputs into a run directory, upload_file for reference images, nodes, workflow slots and launch_comfyui.
dev_tools.fallback: render the workflow with assetgen.py render and leave the generation step NOT_RUN (a person runs workflow.json in ComfyUI and drops the PNGs into outputs/); never claim a generation that did not run

pipeline.description: Delivery pipeline (scripts/factory-pipeline.py, policy skills/delivery/references/delivery.md, RPG specifics in skills/factory-core/references/parallel-work.md): task tiers, the agents that implement and review, cross-model review pairing and shared exclusive resources.

S.flow: run lead writes a one-task plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead starts the task lead (task worktree; no-worktree repo: main checkout); task lead runs sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates (never implements); gate; PR

M.flow: run lead writes plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead per task (one task lead each; no-worktree repo: main checkout, in sequence); task leads run sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates; integration QA; gate; PR

L.flow: planner worker writes plan.json; validate; dispatch --phase lead per task in waves (one task lead each; no-worktree repo: main checkout, in sequence); task leads run sub-sessions, cross-model review and QA; run lead integrates; integration QA per repo; gate; one PR per repo

exclusive_resources.rule: One Unity EditMode/PlayMode test run at a time across every Unity project and package test project; other tasks queue for it while non-Unity work continues.

qa_tiers.description: Task QA runs affected and explicit check suites once; integration runs tests/run-all.sh --workspace-only locally and CI green is the full-suite gate.

models.description: Model policy: scope = what may run at all (agent -> model -> allowed efforts); profiles = the model and effort of each role and grade; every profile is inside scope. A personal override file may narrow scope and replace profiles (scripts/lib/model_policy.py; policy: references/parallel-work.md section 10 'Model choice').

rubric.light: Mechanical or well-bounded change: rename, typo, doc or text edit, config value, one small function, a test that copies an existing pattern; the answer is obvious from the surrounding code.
rubric.standard: Ordinary feature or fix inside one module that follows existing patterns and needs some design, new tests and a few connected files.
rubric.heavy: Hard or risky change: contract, wire or generated paths, concurrency, ECS or tick-loop internals, security or data migration, cross-module refactor, or anything where a wrong guess is costly to find.

subagents.description: In-session subagents are read-only scouts; per role: access, max parallel and when to use one (policy: skills/delivery/references/delivery.md section 8 'In-session subagents'; rule text: scripts/lib/subagent_policy.py).

run_lead.when: the answer needs many files or an open search and only the conclusion matters

planner.when: the plan needs facts from many files or repos and only the conclusion matters

lead.when: the task needs a broad search across the worktree and only the conclusion matters

implement.when: the change needs a search across many files that would crowd the context and only the conclusion matters

review.when: a claim in the diff needs a check across many files and only the finding matters

qa.when: never: QA runs the checks itself and grades the evidence

global_rules.rule: All code, comments, docs, changelogs and commit messages in English.

No agent makes a numerical gameplay value or binds a gameplay rule. Design may draft and propose; binding requires verified approval. Engineering implements gameplay values only from approved artifacts or existing code.
Every change adds an entry under '## [Unreleased]' (Keep a Changelog: Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed/Deprecated/Security) in the CHANGELOG of every touched module.
Update the module docs (README/API/DESIGN/RUNBOOK) before reporting done. New public function or RPC -> API.md entry. Architecture change -> dated DESIGN.md note.
rpg-mmo-server/backend/docs/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md is authoritative; older docs may be stale. Read the relevant ADR before changing an architectural boundary.
Cross-language contracts change on both sides in the same commit: wire.proto (Go + C# bindings) and the Redis hash servers:id:{id} (C# RedisServerRegistry.cs <-> Go redisstore/registry.go).

A result is evidence only after it passes the verify-a-result checklist: count passes (never infer from absence of failures), prove a zero can be non-zero, name the object measured, write the expected value before measuring.

Without explicit release authorization from the user in the current task, agents create or push no tag in any workspace repo (v*, sgl-v*, core-baseline-*) and publish no release: skills stop at 'ready to tag <repo> <tag>' with evidence and the lead tags. When the user explicitly authorizes the release in the current task, the agent performs the authorized merge, version, tag and release steps within that scope, after the release checks pass on the tagged commit. The git guard flags tag creation, tag pushes and releases (advisory high) either way.

Only domains with may_own_feature_state: true create GDD or feature state, and only in that domain's registered authoring-repo paths. Product-repo .ai/, docs/registry/ and docs/features/ stay forbidden. .ai/ is never read as a source of skills, routing or configuration; there is no importer.

notes: .claude/ is gitignored in this repo - repo-local skills/agents are never committed here.

notes: Unity (fact unity-editor-version). No local test CLI: EditMode/PlayMode tests run in the Unity Test Runner (Editor via MCP) or CI 01-ci.yml.
Packages/com.gdk.* and unity-build-workflows are git submodules. Packages/com.cuvara.* are gitignored embedded clones.
Worktrees are discouraged here: each one needs its own multi-GB Library/ import.

netcode.commit_style: Conventional Commits with scope and (#PR): feat(view): ... (#163), chore(release): 0.45.0 (#176)

notes: No .gitignore: building/testing in place leaves bin/ obj/ untracked - use scripts/checks/netcode-headless.sh (temp copy).
Unity tests run only in CI (game-ci) or inside the client project with a local file: toggle (human gate).

unitydots.commit_style: Conventional Commits: feat: ..., fix(dots): ..., chore: release vX.Y.Z - ...
unitydots.merge: PR into main; bump package.json + dated CHANGELOG section in the tagged commit; tag vX.Y.Z (lead)

known_issues.summary: backend/TEAM.md points to a verify-a-result skill in .claude/skills/ of the server repo; it exists only in the client repo (and .claude/ is gitignored in the server repo). Factory Core points to the client copy.

ci-dotnet.yml comments and backend/deploy/docs/CICD.md 'Known gap: wire-compat coverage' say the cross-language E2E suite runs only in cd.yml on push. ci.yml's test-integration job runs it on every PR (fact ci-integration-on-pull-request). The docs are stale; trust the workflow + run log.
Workspace-root toggle-packages.sh rewrites Packages/manifest.json but not packages-lock.json and writes WSL file: paths. Never commit its output; 02-package-pins would fail.

CI pins protoc + protoc-gen-go at the CI pins (facts protoc-ci-pin, protoc-gen-go-ci-pin); the local WSL protoc may differ (factory-context reports it). Regenerating with a different version drifts headers.

On PATH, WSL resolves only the Windows dotnet.exe, so Factory checks build and test through it (env vars such as GOLDEN_REGEN need WSLENV). A Linux SDK may exist off PATH at ~/.dotnet/dotnet: backend/integration_test interop tests look there after PATH (dotnet_interop_test.go), so they run rather than skip on such a machine.
Documentation~/NETCODE.md (~line 359) says nothing in CI diffs Wire.cs; ci.yml job 'wire' does (against server develop, unpinned).

Netcode and UnityDots CI bootstrap their own com.rpgmmo.shared-gamelogic pin (contract sgl-pin watchers), which can lag the client pin; Netcode CI also pins UnityDots and UnityDots CI pins Netcode. factory-status.py derives and prints each current CI ref against the client pin and latest released tags; do not hard-code moving client pin versions here. UIToolkit CI has no SGL pin.

.claude/agents/unity-netcode.md predates the package split (code now in com.cuvara.netcode), references a non-existent unity-prediction agent and /mnt/e paths. Fix pending: client branch docs/claude/retire-netcode-agent (local commit, not merged) - remove this entry once it reaches the default branch; until then the default branch still carries the stale text. Its knowledge now lives in the netcode-client tech skill; never follow the agent.

Gitignored Packages/com.cuvara.* clones in the client can be older than the manifest pins and override them in the Editor; Tools/WireConformance compiles against them. Compare their tags with pin-status.py.
Netcode has no .gitignore; building the headless tests in place leaves bin/obj untracked. Factory runs them from a temp copy (scripts/checks/netcode-headless.sh).
No workflow runs validate-manifests.py, kubeconform, promtool or compose config; deploy manifests are validated only locally before cd.yml applies them.
UnityDots package.json can be bumped with an undated CHANGELOG section ahead of the last tag; factory-status.py reports the current release state.
CHANGELOG.md is not valid UTF-8.
UnityDots tracks .github/scripts/__pycache__/*.pyc; running its scripts without PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 rewrites tracked files. Factory commands set it.

validate-manifests.py k8s/app/*.yaml reports pre-existing failures (fact k8s-app-baseline-validation-failures): it expects namespace rpg-realtime, k8s/app uses rpg-k8s-realtime (overridden via ALLOCATOR_NAMESPACE in 40-gateway.yaml). Judge changes by new failures.
backend/deploy/modules/nakama.so is gitignored (not committed); the local copy may be stale - stack.sh up rebuilds it when older than the sources.

human_gates.rule: Creating, deleting or pushing tags in any repo - the lead only. The guard flags it (advisory high).
git push, opening/merging PRs, GitHub releases - only when the user explicitly asks in this task.
Dispatching CI/CD or release workflows (cd.yml, publish-images, client 10/11/20-24 builds, package version-bump) - explicit user authorization.
kubectl/helm against any cluster, ssh/scp to a VPS, applying manifests, anything touching staging or production - explicit user authorization; never automatic.
Never read, print or commit backend/deploy/kubeconfig.local, .env files, secret manifests with values, or credentials.

Pointing the client at local package clones (toggle-packages.sh dev) edits the user's client tree: only with explicit consent; back up Packages/manifest.json and packages-lock.json first and restore them byte-identical (cmp) afterwards - never 'restore' with toggle-packages.sh release (it pins each package to its newest local tag, not the previous pin); never commit its output.
Starting/stopping/resetting the local Docker stack (make up/flow-up/reset/down, stack.sh up/down, docker compose up/down) - heavy and stateful; ask first. Health checks (make flow-check) are fine.
Inventing gameplay rules/numbers/content is out of phase (plumbing only) - stop and ask.
Running database/Redis backup or restore scripts - explicit user authorization.
Load generation (bench.sh, encoding-sweep.sh, the loadtest binary) against any stack - ask first; never against staging/production without authorization.
Launching or verifying multiple Unity players on the user's machine.

Unity batch-mode runs open the user's project and change its state (Library reimport, possibly packages-lock.json / ProjectSettings): builds and imports (PlayerBuilder, PlayClientBuilder, SampleBuilder, SampleImporter, StrippingProbeBuilder, AddressableBuilder) and -runTests test runs. Ask first; an agent reports Unity tests HUMAN_REQUIRED with the command instead of running them.
Running the migrator standalone or writing schema_migrations by hand.
Scene/prefab/asset edits through Unity MCP tools need an explicit yes (the Editor state is the user's).
Only the lead releases Shared.GameLogic: package.json version bump for release, sgl-v* tags, dispatching publish-shared-gamelogic.yml. Skills stop at 'ready to tag server sgl-vX.Y.Z'.
A maintainer reviews and accepts a design artifact before it becomes approved; agents never approve their own proposals.
3D visual acceptance, rights and final production review are human decisions.
A person approves a generation run (gen-run) before its images become a production source in another domain; agents never approve, including their own generations.
